description: This represents the beginning long-term debt outstanding for non-governmental public debt issued for private purposes. This includes debt such as industrial development bonds, pollution control bonds, and other conduit debt where the government issues bonds on behalf of private entities to finance projects that serve a public purpose but are ultimately the responsibility of the private entity. The debt is considered public because it is issued by a public entity, but it is used to support private sector activities.
tagline: Beginning long-term private purpose public debt.
census_description: Beg LTD O/S-NG-public debt for private purpose

description: This represents the beginning long-term debt outstanding for unspecified public purposes. This includes all long-term debt not classified under other specific categories, providing a catch-all for any miscellaneous long-term obligations held by the government at the start of the fiscal year.

This covers long-term debt issued for non-governmental public debt for private purposes during the fiscal year. This includes the issuance of new bonds by a government entity on behalf of private organizations to fund projects that benefit the public but are managed and financed by the private sector. Examples include industrial development and pollution control projects.
tagline: Issued long-term private purpose public debt.
census_description: LTD Iss-NG-public debt for private purpose

description: This denotes long-term debt issued for unspecified public purposes during the fiscal year. It captures all new long-term obligations not categorized under other specific purposes, serving as a general category for miscellaneous long-term debt issuances.

This refers to the long-term debt retired for non-governmental public debt for private purposes during the fiscal year. It includes payments made to retire or pay off bonds issued by the government on behalf of private entities, marking the reduction of such debt obligations.
tagline: Retired long-term private purpose public debt.
census_description: LTD Ret-NG-public debt for private purpose

description: This represents long-term debt retired for unspecified public purposes during the fiscal year. It includes the repayment or retirement of long-term obligations that do not fall under other specific categories, providing a general classification for miscellaneous debt retirements.

This indicates long-term debt outstanding for non-governmental industrial revenue bonds at the end of the fiscal year. These bonds are issued by a government entity to finance industrial projects carried out by private businesses, with the debt serviced by the revenue generated from those projects rather than tax revenue.

This refers to long-term debt outstanding for unspecified public purposes at the end of the fiscal year. It encompasses all remaining long-term obligations not specifically categorized, providing a broad classification for miscellaneous long-term debt still owed by the government.

This covers the short-term debt outstanding at the beginning of the fiscal year. Short-term debt is defined as interest-bearing obligations payable within one year from the date of issuance, including notes, warrants, and other short-term borrowings.

This represents the short-term debt outstanding at the end of the fiscal year. It includes all interest-bearing short-term obligations that remain unpaid at the fiscal year's conclusion, providing a snapshot of the government's short-term liabilities.
census_description: Short Term Debt O/S-End of FY

This function covers state government direct cash payments to individuals for tuition, scholarships, and other financial aid to meet educational expenses (other than loans). The payments can be based on academic merit, financial need, athletic ability, or educational disadvantage. It also includes direct cash subsidies to private schools and colleges. Specific inclusions are scholarships for specific areas of study (e.g., medicine, dentistry), fellowships, tuition or fee aid, credits, waivers, remissions, trainee stipends, student prizes, state veterans educational opportunity grants, and financial aid to private or parochial schools and colleges.

This function encompasses expenditures associated with federal categorical assistance programs, specifically Supplemental Security Income (SSI), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), and the Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). It includes state-to-Federal intergovernmental payments on behalf of SSI recipients and cash payments to families under the TANF program. It excludes cash payments to needy persons under programs other than SSI and TANF and intergovernmental payments to finance locally-administered assistance programs other than TANF and Medicaid.

This function involves cash payments made directly to individuals based on their financial need, excluding those under Federal categorical assistance programs. It includes poor relief, general relief, home relief, emergency relief, general assistance, refugee assistance, medical assistance, housing expense relief, and energy assistance (e.g., LIHEAP). The assistance must be paid directly to individuals and not to vendors, and covers other direct assistance to needy persons not eligible for Federal categorical assistance. This function excludes administration of such programs and payments made to vendors rather than individuals.

description: Taxes imposed on ownership of property and measured by its value. This includes general property taxes on real and personal property, special property taxes on selected types of property, and taxes based on income produced by property as a measure of its value on the assessment date. Penalties and interest on delinquent property taxes, proceeds of tax sales, and tax redemptions up to the amount of taxes due plus penalties and interest are also included.

Taxes applicable with specified exceptions to sales of all types of goods and services or to all gross receipts, whether at a single rate or at classified rates. This includes sales or gross receipts taxes on the purchase or lease of motor vehicles if there is no specific and separate tax law covering this activity.
Taxes on the sale of alcoholic beverages, whether collected through government-operated liquor stores or through private outlets.
Taxes on admission tickets or admission charges and on gross receipts of all or specified types of amusement businesses.
Taxes imposed distinctively on insurance companies and measured by gross premiums or adjusted gross premiums.

Taxes on gasoline, diesel oil, aviation fuel, “gasohol,” “ethanol,” and any other fuels used in motor vehicles or aircraft. Excludes taxes on sale of fuels other than motor fuels and refunds of fuel taxes.

Taxes measured by amounts wagered or bet on horse-racing, dog racing, jai-lai, etc., including “breakage” collected by the government. Excludes race track licenses not based on amounts wagered and sales taxes on race track admissions.

Taxes imposed distinctively on public utilities and measured by gross receipts, gross earnings, or units of service sold, either as a direct tax on consumers or as a percentage of gross receipts of the utility. Includes public utilities like transportation companies, telephone, telegraph, cable television providers, and Internet service providers.
Taxes on tobacco products and synthetic cigars and cigarettes, including related products like cigarette tubes and paper.

Taxes on specific commodities, businesses, or services not reported separately above. Includes taxes on contractors, hotel/motel, lubricating oil, fuels other than motor fuel, motor vehicles, meals, soft drinks, margarine, etc. For state governments, includes sales or use taxes based on sales price where the authorizing legislation is separate from the state’s general sales and use tax law.

Licenses for manufacturing, importing, wholesaling, and retailing of alcoholic beverages. Excludes taxes based on volume or value of transactions and Federal customs duties on alcoholic beverage imports.

Licenses on amusement businesses generally and on specific types of amusement enterprises or devices like race tracks, movie theaters, athletic events, pinball and video game machines, etc. Excludes licenses based on value or number of admissions, amount of wagers, or gross or net income and receipts.

Franchise license taxes; organization, filing, and entrance fees; taxes on property measured by amount of corporate stock, debt, or other basis besides assessed value of property; and other licenses applicable with few, specified exceptions to all corporations. Excludes taxes on corporations based on value of property, net income, or gross receipts from sales.
Licenses for commercial and noncommercial hunting and fishing permits.

Licenses imposed on owners or operators of motor vehicles for the right to use public highways, such as fees for title registration, license plates, vehicle inspection, vehicle mileage and weight taxes on motor carriers, highway use taxes, and off-highway fees. Excludes personal property taxes on motor vehicles, sales or gross receipts taxes on the sale of motor vehicles, and other taxes on the business of motor transport.
Licenses for the privilege of driving motor vehicles, both commercial and private.

Licenses distinctively imposed on public utilities, whether privately- or publicly-owned. Includes public utilities like transportation companies, telephone, telegraph, cable television providers, and Internet service providers.

Licenses (including examination and inspection fees) required of persons engaged in particular professions, trades, or occupations; taxes on insurance companies based on value of their policies; such taxes on businesses not elsewhere classified; and charges or fees relating to the inspection and marketing of commodities.

Licenses not listed separately above, such as animal licenses, health permits, marriage licenses, building and equipment permits, individual permits to purchase liquor, registration fees on aircraft and pleasure boats, impact fees paid in connection with issuance of building permits, and other nonbusiness privileges.

Taxes on individuals measured by net income and taxes on special types of income like interest, dividends, income from intangible property, etc. For local governments, includes wages, salaries, and other compensation earned by both residents and nonresidents.

Taxes on corporations and unincorporated businesses (when taxed separately from individual income), measured by net income, whether on corporations in general or on specific kinds of corporations like financial institutions. Excludes income taxes on gross income or receipts of corporations.
Taxes imposed on the transfer of property at death, in contemplation of death, or as a gift (e.g., inheritance and estate taxes).
Taxes on the recording, registration, and transfer of documents like mortgages, deeds, and securities. Excludes taxes on recording or transfer of motor vehicle titles.

Taxes imposed distinctively on removal (severance) of natural resources like oil, gas, coal, other minerals, timber, fish, etc. from land or water and measured by the value or quantity of products removed or sold.

Taxes not listed separately or provided for in categories above, such as taxes on land at a specified rate per acre rather than on assessed value. Examples include local governments imposing a “Per Capita Tax” based strictly on residency within a community.

Compulsory contributions and reimbursements from owners of property who benefit from specific public improvements, such as street paving, sidewalks, highway construction, sewer lines, and drainage projects. Excludes proceeds from sale of special assessment bonds and maintenance assessments for recurrent services like street lighting.

Amounts received from the sale of real property, buildings, improvements to them, land easements, rights-of-way, and other capital assets. Includes proceeds from the sale of land and improvements associated with housing and community development programs, and sale of toll roads.

Amounts from interest on all interest-bearing deposits and accounts, accrued interest on investment securities sold, interest on funds held for construction, and interest related to public debt for private purposes. Excludes interest on deposits and investments of employee retirement and other insurance trust funds, and recorded profits on sale of investments.

Revenue from penalties imposed for violations of law; civil penalties; court fees if levied upon conviction of a crime or violation; court-ordered restitutions to crime victims; and forfeits of deposits held for performance guarantees or against loss or damage. Excludes penalties relating to tax delinquency, library fines, and sale of confiscated property.

Revenue from allowing temporary possession of government-owned buildings, land, or other fixed properties. Includes grazing fees, timberland leases, rental of unused land or property, and revenue from leases relating to natural resource exploration and production. Excludes rental revenue from functionally classified facilities and rental revenue from other governments.

Compensation or portion of proceeds received by a state or local government for granting the privilege of using or developing property or operating under a right, primarily those related to natural resources like oil, gas, and mineral rights. Excludes sale of timber and other forestry products from state forests.
Gifts of cash or securities from private individuals or corporations. Excludes noncash gifts and donations like food, property, buildings, land, commodities, etc.
Proceeds from the operation of government-sponsored lotteries after deducting the cost of prizes. This includes amounts used for administration reported at Administrative Expenses.

Recovery of losses charged off in a prior fiscal year, insurance adjustments, payments-in-lieu-of-taxes from private sources, voluntary contributions or reimbursements to defray construction costs of capital improvement projects, premiums on bonds issued, revenues from sponsorship agreements, unemployment compensation contributions from employers for servicing debt issued to cover

Cash and security holdings specifically for debt service purposes, including interest payments and redemption of principal on long-term debt. This includes cash on hand with fiscal agents for debt service or for redemption of uncanceled debt, bond reserve funds, balances in refunding bond accounts held pending completion of refunding transactions, and credit paper or other assets pledged to the ultimate redemption of debt.

Cash and security holdings of accounting funds established specifically to hold proceeds of bond issues (and related revenues) pending their disbursement. This includes various cash and security assets, excluding capital project funds whose sources of revenue do not include proceeds of bond issues and proceeds of public debt for private purposes not yet distributed.

Cash and security holdings of funds and other accounts except those cited in other specific categories, including utilities and liquor stores. This includes various cash and security assets, excluding cash and security holdings of social insurance trust systems.

Payroll levies (or “taxes”) collected from private and public employers (and in some cases employees) to provide for unemployment compensation benefits. This includes funds used to pay regular benefits to eligible individuals who are temporarily out of work and seeking employment.

Interest earned on deposits held in the Unemployment Trust Fund of the U.S. Treasury and credited to individual state governments and the District of Columbia. This includes accrued interest on deposits and other interest-bearing accounts held within the Unemployment Trust Fund.

Net amounts credited to the accounts of individual state governments and the District of Columbia during periods when contributions and interest are insufficient to pay benefits. This involves advances and contributions provided by the federal government to support state-administered unemployment compensation programs.

Basic payments to individuals temporarily out of work and seeking employment, funded by state payroll taxes and to former Federal civilian and military employees, funded by Federal agencies that employed them. This covers regular benefits distributed to eligible recipients under the cooperative Federal-state unemployment compensation insurance programs.

Payments for extended unemployment benefits in states with high rates of unemployment, funded equally by Federal and state payroll taxes. This includes benefits under special programs, such as trade adjustment assistance, disaster assistance, and benefits to special groups of former workers, such as railroad employees.
Balance held in each state’s basic trust fund account in the U.S. Treasury. This represents the total amount of funds available within the trust fund account for unemployment compensation purposes.

Other balances in clearing and benefit accounts of the U.S. Treasury for unemployment compensation systems. This can be a positive or negative number, reflecting the net balance during periods of higher than normal unemployment when states may borrow from the Federal Government to cover benefits.

Premiums, assessments, payroll taxes, or other contributions collected from employers and employees to provide for workers’ compensation benefits, including contributions from local governments as employers on behalf of their employees.

Interest earnings on investment securities, deposits, and other interest-bearing accounts, including accrued interest on investment securities sold, dividends, recorded profits on investment transactions (minus any recorded losses), rentals, and other earnings on investments.

Claims paid directly to, or on behalf of, injured beneficiaries for compensation of wages lost, medical care, rehabilitation, funeral expenses, and other eligible benefits. This includes payments made from regular workers’ compensation funds as well as from subsequent injury funds and similar sources.
Cash and security holdings of state government compulsory accident and injury insurance systems for workers’ compensation. This includes various cash and security assets held by these systems.

Premiums, assessments, or contributions collected from members to provide for benefits under state-administered social insurance systems for health benefits, disability benefits, and other purposes. This includes contributions from local governments as employers on behalf of their own employees.

Interest earnings on investment securities, deposits, and other interest-bearing accounts for other state-administered social insurance trust systems. This includes accrued interest on investment securities sold, dividends, recorded profits on investment transactions, rentals, and other earnings on investments.

Distribution of cash benefits to eligible persons under state-administered plans for compulsory or voluntary social insurance programs not elsewhere classified. This includes claims paid directly to, or on behalf of, beneficiaries for lost income, medical care, disaster reimbursement, and other eligible expenses.

Cash and security holdings of state government insurance trust systems other than employee retirement, unemployment compensation, and workers’ compensation. This includes various cash and security assets held by these systems.

Total expenditure during the fiscal year for salaries and wages, covering all functions and activities of the government and its dependent agencies. This includes gross amounts paid for compensation of officers and employees before deductions for taxes, retirement contributions, subsistence charges, or other purposes.
